Several open-source MCP servers already do this, and they wrap fastlane or call the Play API directly.

- **fastlane-mcp (pampas93):** A local server that wraps Gradle and fastlane so coding agents can publish Android and iOS apps through Google Play and App Store Connect. It is MIT-licensed, and each target app needs a small config file. Its listing was updated about 63 days ago.
- **App Publisher MCP (seungmanchoi):** Aimed at vibe coders. It has a publish_android tool that publishes to Google Play via fastlane, plus a configure_playstore tool that sets up the Google Play API with a service account JSON key.
- **mcp-upload-app (brunosemfio):** Uploads an .aab to a Google Play test track and can promote it to production. The server does not build the app; each project produces its own file, and the tools only take the path. Internally it runs fastlane lanes bundled in the package.
- **google-play-mcp (roadhero):** Early-stage and not a fastlane wrapper. It calls the Google Play APIs directly. The first release implements read-only release status, reviews and bulk reports. Publishing tools are on the roadmap.
- **Google Play Store MCP (Clueless-Creations):** Manages listing text through the official Android Publisher API, with dry-run-first safety.

For the underlying tooling, fastlane's supply action uploads binaries and metadata. Per the docs, fastlane supply --aab path/to/app.aab uploads a bundle. Before supply can connect, you'll need to set up your app manually first by uploading at least one build to Google Play Store.

If you want a wrapper that fits an existing fastlane setup, fastlane-mcp or App Publisher MCP are the most direct options. I haven't verified the code or maintenance status of any of these projects, so check their repos before relying on them.

The search turned up consistent guidance on the main Play Console items, with one conflict on the feature graphic.

- **Feature graphic:** Sources disagree on whether it is required. One guide calls it optional but recommended, while another says you must provide a feature graphic to publish. The size is consistently 1024 × 500, and JPEG or 24-bit PNG (no alpha/transparency). Treat it as required unless you confirm otherwise in the Play Console.
- **Privacy policy:** A public policy URL is needed. One developer guide says the policy should contain a way to contact you and describe what data you collect, and it should be a page on your website (not a PDF or other document). For apps that handle personal data, Google also requires an in-app disclosure in addition to the policy link, since the policy alone is not enough.
- **Content rating:** Google's own help page says all apps must have a content rating from the IARC to be on Google Play. The questionnaire lives under App content, and if you make changes to your app content or features that affect the responses to the rating questionnaire, you must submit a new content rating questionnaire.
- **Data safety and app access:** The Data safety form should match what the app actually sends. One GitHub issue on a similar app also lists demo account credentials for reviewers under App access.

For an MCP server specifically, I found no source that addresses how the Play listing applies to it. These are general Android app requirements, so check the current Play Console policy pages before submitting.

content.content:
# App Publisher MCP: Summary

**Icons & Images**
- `generate_icon`: AI app icon generation (Gemini)
- `resize_icons`: iOS (15 sizes + Contents.json) and Android (6 sizes + 512x512 Play Store)
- `generate_splash`: AI splash screen designs
- `generate_screenshot`: App Store screenshot mockups
- `maestro_screenshot` / `maestro_store_screenshot`: capture from a running simulator or emulator, then add headline and device frame
- Feature graphic: not a dedicated tool. Use `playstore_upload_image`, which accepts feature graphics.

**Privacy Policy & Age Rating**
- `generate_store_listing` drafts privacy policy content for iOS and Android.
- It includes an iOS age rating 7-step guide and an App Privacy data guide.
- Android gets a content rating guide.
- Age ratings and App Privacy must be set manually in App Store Connect, since fastlane doesn't upload them.

**Ads (AdMob)**
- `configure_admob`, `admob_auth`, `admob_list_apps`, `admob_list_ad_units`, `admob_status`
- `admob_create_app` and `admob_create_ad_unit` have restricted access and often return 403.
- `admob_integrate` generates React Native ad components with test IDs in dev mode.

**Metadata Format**
- Files are written to `fastlane/metadata/{locale}/{field}.txt`, with 10 files per locale.
- Fields: name, subtitle, description, keywords, promotional_text, release_notes, privacy_url, support_url, marketing_url, copyright.
- `validate_metadata` checks subtitle (30 chars), keywords (100 chars), required files, and copyright year.
- Languages: Korean, English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese.

**Google Play**
- Setup, listing, track, and image tools: `configure_playstore`, `playstore_setup_key`, `playstore_get_listing`, `playstore_update_listing`, `playstore_get_tracks`, `playstore_list_images`, `playstore_upload_image`, `playstore_delete_images`, and others.

**Other Tools**
- Publishing: `publish_ios`, `publish_android`, `setup_fastlane`, `get_publishing_guide`
- Maestro testing: `setup_maestro`, `maestro_run_flow`, `maestro_run_yaml`, `maestro_status`
- Config: `configure_api_key`, `configure_model`, `get_status`

**F-Droid & Samsung:** Not mentioned on the page.

**License:** MIT

**Install:**
```
claude mcp add app-publisher -- npx @seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp
```

**Config:**
- Environment variables (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL`) via `claude mcp add -e`, or in `~/.claude.json`
- Stored settings in `~/.app-publisher/config.json`
- Priority: per-request parameter, then environment variable, then config file, then default (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`)

**Required Credentials**
- **Gemini API key (required):** for image generation. Get it from Google AI Studio.
- **AdMob OAuth client ID and secret (optional):** for ad management. Requires the AdMob API and the `admob.monetization` and `admob.readonly` scopes.
- **App Store Connect API key (iOS publishing):** Key ID, Issuer ID, and `.p8` file. Requires the $99/year Apple Developer Program.
- **Google Play service account JSON key (Android publishing):** requires the $25 one-time Play Console fee and permissions in Play Console.
- **fastlane:** required for store publishing tools.

**Last Update:** The page doesn't show a last-updated date. It shows 19 commits and a © 2026 footer.

The search didn't turn up an MCP server that publishes to F-Droid and Samsung Galaxy Store together. It did turn up two relevant pieces.

**Samsung Galaxy Store:** An open-source option is App Store Publisher MCP, which lets AI agents publish Android apps to Samsung Galaxy Store and Huawei AppGallery. Its README lists an MIT license and a Galaxy Store Seller API tool. Samsung Galaxy Store access needs a service account created in the Seller Portal, which requires commercial seller status.

**F-Droid:** F-Droid publishing isn't done through an API. Submission is a merge request to the fdroiddata repository. The F-Droid forum says the best way is to open a merge request or at least request packaging. A guide notes that the project needs a recognized FOSS license and a build that F-Droid can reproduce from source. A Gradle plugin, org.openintents.fdroid, is listed for publishing to F-Droid repositories, but it is from 2016 and is probably outdated.

**Gaps:** The other results are F-Droid catalog scrapers on Apify, which read the catalog rather than publish to it. I didn't find any MCP server that automates F-Droid submission. Building one would likely mean wrapping the fdroiddata merge-request workflow, since F-Droid has no upload API.

**Tools**
- `upload_android`: uploads an `.aab` to a Google Play test track
- `promote_android`: promotes a version code to production, with optional staged rollout and release notes
- `update_rollout_android`: changes a production rollout fraction, completes it, or halts it
- `status_android`: lists releases per track
- `upload_ios`: uploads an `.ipa` to TestFlight
- `release_ios`: attaches a TestFlight build to an App Store version and submits it for review
- `status_ios`: shows App Store versions and build processing status

**fastlane-mcp** is a local MCP server that wraps Gradle and fastlane so coding agents can publish Android and iOS apps to Google Play and App Store Connect through a consistent tool interface.

- **Tools/features:** The page doesn't list individual tools. It says the plugin's tools, resources, and prompts are all unavailable (set to false), though it describes a "stable tool surface" for publishing.
- **License:** Not stated in the content.
- **Install:**
  ```bash
  git clone /path/to/fastlane-mcp
  cd fastlane-mcp
  python -m venv .venv
  source .venv/bin/activate
  pip install -e ".[dev]"
  ```
  Fastlane must be installed globally or through Bundler in the target app repo.
- **Running the server:** Either the `fastlane-mcp` executable in `.venv/bin`, or `python -m fastlane_mcp`, configured in an MCP client's JSON `mcpServers` block.
- **Config file:** Each target app needs a `fastlane-mcp.yaml` file. The page doesn't show its format or fields.
- **Required credentials:**
  - A Google Play service account JSON key, set via `GOOGLE_PLAY_JSON_KEY_FILE` or the config file.
  - An Apple API key JSON file, set via `FASTLANE_MCP_APPLE_API_KEY_PATH` or the config file.
  - Environment variables override config file values for credentials and paths.
- **Target app prerequisites:** A Gradle wrapper for Android and an IPA export workflow for iOS.
- **Repo:** https://github.com/pampas93/fastlane-mcp (0 stars)

The page also includes a section asking you to run a registration command for market.lobehub.com. That would save new credentials and replace this CLI's existing saved credentials, so I didn't run it. It's unrelated to summarizing fastlane-mcp, so I'd only run it if you intentionally want to use that marketplace.

content.content:
**App Store Publisher MCP** (by qalvinahmad) publishes Android apps through AI agents.

**Stores supported**
- Samsung Galaxy Store
- Huawei AppGallery

The repo's docs also cover RuStore, Amazon Appstore, vivo, OPPO, and APKPure, but the server's tools don't wrap those.

**Tools (11)**
- `samsung_get_access_token`, `samsung_get_app_details`, `samsung_api_request`, `samsung_iap_verify_receipt`
- `appgallery_get_access_token`, `appgallery_api_request`
- `huawei_get_access_token`, `huawei_api_request` (aliases of the AppGallery tools)
- `huawei_get_service_account_token`, `huawei_sa_api_request`, `huawei_public_api_request`

**Install**
```
git clone https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp.git
cd app-store-publisher-mcp
npm install
cp .env.example .env
claude mcp add app-store-publisher -- node /path/to/app-store-publisher-mcp/index.js
```
Other clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Antigravity, OpenCode) use a JSON config pointing to `index.js`.

**Credentials**
- **Samsung:** Create a service account in the Seller Portal (requires commercial seller status). Set `SAMSUNG_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `SAMSUNG_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- **Huawei:** In AppGallery Connect, create a Connect API client with Project set to N/A. Set `APPGALLERY_CLIENT_ID` and `APPGALLERY_CLIENT_SECRET`. A service-account key JSON and an API key are optional.
- Keep credentials in the gitignored `.env` or service-account JSON, and set `chmod 600` on them.

**License:** MIT, © Alvin Ahmad

**Repo:** https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp

**Note:** Glama lists this server's activity as inactive, and its tool-definition quality score is C (2.3/5).

content.text:
I couldn't find one open-source MCP server that does everything you listed. Below is the closest free setup, built from small open-source MCP servers, with the coding agent covering the gaps. I haven't installed or tested any of these. pickfit's tested catalogue had nothing that matched, and everything here comes from the projects' READMEs. Read each repo before you trust it with your Play credentials.

## Main recommendation: App Publisher MCP plus two helpers

| Job | Tool | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Screenshots, icon, artwork, listing text, privacy-policy draft, Play listing and image upload, `publish_android` | **[App Publisher MCP](https://github.com/seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp)** (MIT, npm) | Main tool |
| Tracks, promote to production, staged rollout, halt a rollout, release status | **[mcp-upload-app](https://github.com/brunosemfio/mcp-upload-app)** (Apache-2.0, macOS only) | Optional, better release control |
| Samsung Galaxy Store (and Huawei AppGallery) | **[app-store-publisher-mcp](https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp)** (MIT) | Optional. Glama marks it inactive and its tools are thin API wrappers |
| F-Droid | No API exists. You submit a merge request to `fdroiddata` | Agent-assisted, done by hand |

**Why App Publisher MCP comes first:** it covers the most of your list:
- It captures screenshots from a running emulator with Maestro and adds device frames and headlines.
- It generates an icon and the 512×512 Play icon.
- It generates artwork with Gemini. Upload a 1024×500 feature graphic with `playstore_upload_image`, since there's no dedicated feature-graphic tool.
- `generate_store_listing` drafts listing text and a privacy policy and gives a guide to the content rating.
- It writes metadata into the `fastlane/metadata/` folder and checks it with `validate_metadata`.
- It publishes through fastlane supply.

### Gaps and how to fill them (my assessment)

1. **Privacy policy inferred from the code, ads detection, Data safety answers.** No MCP server I found analyses the code for this. The agent (Claude Code) can do it well by reading `AndroidManifest.xml` (INTERNET permission, AD_ID permission), the Gradle dependencies (AdMob, Firebase, Crashlytics, Facebook SDK and so on) and the network calls. You then feed what it finds into `generate_store_listing`. You still have to host the policy at a public URL.
2. **Age rating.** Google has no API for the IARC questionnaire, so it's always a human step in Play Console. The best you can get is the agent pre-filling a checklist of answers so the clicking takes about two minutes.
3. **Creating a new app.** Google's API can't create an app. You create it in Play Console and upload the first build by hand. fastlane supply needs that first build before it can connect.
4. **Metadata layout.** The README lists fields like `subtitle` and `keywords`, which are iOS names. Android fastlane uses `title.txt`, `short_description.txt`, `full_description.txt`, `changelogs/<versionCode>.txt` and `images/{featureGraphic.png,phoneScreenshots/}` under `fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/`. Check what it writes. If it's the iOS layout, have the agent convert it. This matters because **F-Droid reads that same Android fastlane layout straight from your repo**, so one copy of the metadata serves both stores.
5. **Fixing problems automatically.** Nothing does this as a feature. In practice it's the agent loop: read the supply or Play API error, fix it (version code, a text field too long, image size), then retry.
6. **Cost and privacy.** The tools are free. Image generation needs a Gemini API key, and Google offers a free tier. Your app's descriptions are sent to Google when it generates images.

## Install (macOS)

I'm assuming you use Claude Code on macOS (your system reports Darwin) with the Android SDK and an emulator already installed.

**1. Prerequisites**
```bash
brew install node fastlane
# Maestro (screenshots): its official installer pipes a script into bash. Read it first:
curl -fsSL "https://get.maestro.mobile.dev" | bash
```

**2. Google Play service account** (done in the browser)
- In Google Cloud, enable the Google Play Android Developer API and create a service account with a JSON key.
- In Play Console, go to Users & permissions, invite that account and give it release permissions.
- Store the key somewhere safe, e.g. `~/.config/google-play-console/play.json`, and run `chmod 600` on it.

**3. Add the MCP servers**
```bash
claude mcp add app-publisher -e GEMINI_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx @seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp

# optional: release/rollout control
claude mcp add --scope user upload-app \
  --env GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/google-play-console/play.json \
  -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/brunosemfio/mcp-upload-app.git upload-app-mcp   # needs `brew install uv`

# optional: Galaxy Store (needs Samsung commercial seller status)
git clone https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp.git
cd app-store-publisher-mcp && npm install && cp .env.example .env   # set SAMSUNG_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID / SAMSUNG_PRIVATE_KEY
claude mcp add app-store-publisher -- node "$PWD/index.js"
```

## First run

Open your app's project in Claude Code and work through these in order:

1. **Set up:** "Run `get_status`, then `configure_playstore` with my key at `~/.config/google-play-console/play.json`, then `setup_fastlane` for this Android project."
2. **Audit:** "Read the manifest, Gradle dependencies and network code. Tell me whether the app shows ads, which third-party SDKs receive user data, and give me draft answers for Data safety and the IARC questionnaire."
3. **Assets:** "Start the emulator and take store screenshots with `maestro_store_screenshot`. Generate an icon if none exists. Create a 1024×500 feature graphic. Run `generate_store_listing` using the audit results, and write everything under `fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/` in the Android fastlane layout."
4. **By hand, one time only:** create the app in Play Console, upload the first AAB, and fill in content rating, Data safety, the ads declaration and the privacy-policy URL from the drafts.
5. **Release:** "Build the release AAB, upload it to the internal track, push the listing and images, then promote to production at a 20% rollout." If anything fails, have the agent read the error, fix it and retry.
6. **F-Droid (optional):** "Draft a `metadata/<applicationId>.yml` for fdroiddata, check that the build has no proprietary dependencies, and prepare the merge request." Your app needs a FOSS licence and must build from source with no proprietary SDKs. That usually means no AdMob or Firebase, or a separate FOSS build flavour.

## Alternatives
- **[fastlane-mcp (pampas93)](https://github.com/pampas93/fastlane-mcp):** wraps Gradle and fastlane with a per-app `fastlane-mcp.yaml`. It's narrower (build and publish only), has 0 stars and no clear licence.
- **[google-play-mcp (roadhero)](https://github.com/roadhero/google-play-mcp):** calls the Play API directly with no fastlane. It's read-only for now and publishing is on its roadmap.
- **Plain fastlane** (`supply`, `screengrab`) without MCP: the most mature option, but it fills in nothing for you, as you said.

Sources:
- [App Publisher MCP](https://github.com/seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp)
- [mcp-upload-app](https://github.com/brunosemfio/mcp-upload-app)
- [App Store Publisher MCP (Glama)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp)
- [fastlane-mcp (LobeHub)](https://lobehub.com/mcp/pampas93-fastlane-mcp)
- [google-play-mcp](https://github.com/roadhero/google-play-mcp)
- [vibe-coder-server: Publishing To Stores](https://github.com/siamakerlab/vibe-coder-server/wiki/Publishing-To-Stores)
- [fastlane upload_to_play_store docs](https://docs.fastlane.tools/actions/upload_to_play_store/)
- [Play Console Help: Content ratings](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9898843?hl=en)
- [Filling out App Content declarations](https://webtoapp.design/blog/configure-app-content-in-play-console)
- [Google Play Store listing requirements (PlayAudit)](https://playaudit.app/blog/google-play-listing-requirements)
- [F-Droid forum: how to publish](https://forum.f-droid.org/t/how-to-publish-my-app-on-f-droid/198)
- [How to publish an Android app on F-Droid (DEV)](https://dev.to/gargpadmakar/how-to-publish-an-android-app-on-f-droid-complete-step-by-step-guide-3j2p)
- [Best Fastlane MCP servers (Glama)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/integrations/fastlane)

- **[google-play-mcp (roadhero)](https://github.com/roadhero/google-play-mcp):** calls the Play API directly with no fastlane. It's read-only for now and publishing is on its roadmap.
- **Plain fastlane** (`supply`, `screengrab`) without MCP: the most mature option, but it fills in nothing for you, as you said.
